examples.ko: 우리 팀에는 거포 타자가 한 명 있어요.
examples.en: Our team has one big slugger.
That player grew into a power hitter this year.

examples.ko: 거포가 들어오면서 팀 득점이 크게 늘었어요.
examples.en: Since the slugger joined, the team's scoring has gone up a lot.
Even if he's a slugger, too many strikeouts are a problem.

examples.ko: 그는 홈런을 마흔 개나 친 리그 최고의 거포예요.
examples.en: He is the league's top slugger, with forty home runs.

examples.ko: 이번 시즌에 거포 유망주가 많이 나왔어요.
examples.en: Many promising sluggers appeared this season.

explain: 야구에서 홈런을 펑펑 치는 타자를 말할 때 주로 써요. 정확하게 안타를 치는 '교타자'와 반대 느낌이고, 스포츠 뉴스에서 '거포 유망주'처럼 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 팀은 거포 유망주를 여러 명 키우고 있어요.
phrases.en: That team is developing several promising sluggers.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구 뉴스에서 홈런을 많이 칠 것 같은 젊은 선수를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in baseball news for a young player expected to hit many home runs.

phrases.example: 그는 정확하기보다 힘이 센 거포형 타자예요.
phrases.en: He is a power-type hitter rather than a precise one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-형'이 붙으면 타자의 스타일을 설명하는 느낌이 돼요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-형' describes the hitter's style or type.

phrases.example: 그 선수는 몇 년 만에 거포가 됐어요.
phrases.en: That player became a slugger in a few years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선수가 성장해서 홈런을 많이 치게 된 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a player who has grown into a home run hitter.

explain_en: It is mostly used in baseball for a batter who hits lots of home runs. It contrasts with a '교타자', a contact hitter, and appears in sports news in phrases like '거포 유망주' (slugger prospect).

en: to be renewed; to be updated

examples.ko: 올해 여름 최고 기온 기록이 경신됐어요.
examples.en: This summer's record high temperature was broken.
The world record in track and field was broken again.

examples.ko: 판매 기록이 경신될 때마다 직원들이 기뻐해요.
examples.en: Every time the sales record is broken, the staff are happy.

examples.ko: 이 영화의 관객 수 기록은 곧 경신될 거예요.
examples.en: This movie's attendance record will be broken soon.

examples.ko: 기록이 경신된 날 선수들은 눈물을 흘렸어요.
examples.en: On the day the record was broken, the players cried.

examples.ko: 최저 기온 기록이 경신돼서 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: The record low temperature was broken and it was on the news.

explain: 거의 항상 '기록'과 같이 써서 '기록이 경신되다'라고 해요. 기록을 깨는 사람이 주어이면 '기록을 경신하다'가 돼요. 일상에서는 '기록이 깨지다'가 더 흔해요. 계약이나 여권을 새로 바꾸는 것은 소리가 비슷한 '갱신하다'라고 해서 달라요.

phrases.en: That athlete broke the world record.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기록을 깨는 사람이 주어일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the person who breaks the record is the subject.

phrases.en: This summer's heat record was broken.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고 일상 대화에서 더 자연스러운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning and more natural in everyday talk.
phrases.en_equiv: for a record to be broken

phrases.example: 이번 대회에서 기록이 경신될 것 같아요.
phrases.en: It looks like the record will be broken at this contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~ㄹ 것 같다'로 앞으로의 일을 짐작할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses -ㄹ 것 같다 to guess about something that may happen.
phrases.en_equiv: it seems the record will be renewed

explain_en: It almost always goes with 기록, as in '기록이 경신되다'. When the person who breaks it is the subject, it becomes '기록을 경신하다'. In daily talk '기록이 깨지다' is more common. Renewing a contract or passport uses the similar-sounding but different word '갱신하다'.

examples.en: That writer won a literary award this year.
I bought the award-winning book at the bookstore.
Our school gives a literary award to students every year.

examples.ko: 제 꿈은 신인 문학상에 당선되는 거예요.
examples.en: My dream is to win a new writers' literary award.

examples.ko: 문학상 후보에 오른 소설을 읽고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm reading a novel nominated for the literary award.

examples.ko: 이번 문학상은 시 부문 심사가 어려웠대요.
examples.en: I heard judging the poetry category was hard for this award.

explain: '문학상을 받다', '문학상에 당선되다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 달라요. '노벨 문학상'처럼 이름 앞에 붙여서 말해요. 시, 소설 같은 글을 쓰는 사람이 받는 상이에요.

phrases.en: That writer won the Nobel Prize in Literature.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상 이름 앞에 붙여 가장 유명한 문학상을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put before the prize name to refer to the most famous literary award.

phrases.en: This year's literary award winner was announced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상을 받은 사람을 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person who won the award.

phrases.en: His novel won a literary award.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글을 내서 뽑혔을 때는 '받다'보다 '당선되다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: For a submitted work being chosen, use '당선되다' instead of '받다'.

explain_en: The verbs change with context: 문학상을 받다 for receiving it, 문학상에 당선되다 for winning a contest. It attaches to names, as in 노벨 문학상. It is given to people who write poetry, fiction, and similar works.

en: to be excavated; to be dug

examples.en: The ruins of an ancient city were excavated from underground.
Old bowls were unearthed during construction.
New talent gets discovered at this contest.
Excavated relics are displayed in the museum.
There are many tombs that haven't been excavated yet.
That singer was discovered on the street and became famous.

explain: 땅속의 유물이나 숨은 재능을 찾아 드러낼 때 써요. '발견되다'는 우연히 보게 된 느낌이고, '발굴되다'는 파거나 찾는 노력 끝에 나온다는 느낌이에요. 사람에게는 '발탁되다'와도 비교해 보세요.

phrases.en: New talent was discovered at the audition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숨은 재능 있는 사람을 찾아낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone with hidden talent is found.

phrases.example: 그 지역에서 옛 유물이 계속 발굴되고 있어요.
phrases.en: Old relics are still being excavated in that area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작업이 아직 진행 중일 때 '-고 있다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add '-고 있다' when the work is still in progress.

phrases.en: That tomb has not been excavated yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 파거나 찾아내지 못했을 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used when it has not yet been dug up or found.

explain_en: It is used when relics underground or hidden talent are found and brought out. 발견되다 feels like something noticed by chance; 발굴되다 comes after digging or searching effort. For people, compare it with 발탁되다.

examples.ko: 기자는 불이 난 현장의 상황을 생중계하고 있어요.
examples.en: The reporter is broadcasting the situation at the fire scene live.
The broadcaster airs the final live from start to finish.
Today's opening ceremony was also broadcast live online.
The mayor decided to broadcast the meeting live.
They will broadcast the concert live on this channel.

examples.ko: 현장을 생중계하면 많은 사람이 바로 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you broadcast the scene live, many people can watch right away.

explain: '경기를 생중계하다', '행사를 생중계하다'처럼 현장에서 일어나는 일을 그 자리에서 바로 보여 준다는 느낌으로 써요. '생중계를 하다'로 나누어 말해도 같은 뜻이에요. 방송국, 기자, 개인 채널 모두 주어가 될 수 있어요.

phrases.en: Please broadcast this event live.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부탁할 때 쓰는 말이에요. 표제어는 기본형이라서 말할 때는 이렇게 활용해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to make a polite request; the headword is the dictionary form.

phrases.en: The station broadcast the opening ceremony live yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 끝난 일을 말할 때 쓰는 과거형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Past tense for something that has already happened.

phrases.en: I can see the reporter broadcasting live from the scene.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding -는 lets it modify a following noun.

explain_en: It is used for showing what is happening on the spot right away, as in '경기를 생중계하다' or '행사를 생중계하다'. You can split it as '생중계를 하다' with the same meaning. The subject can be a broadcaster, a reporter or a personal channel.

en: to be owned; to be kept

examples.en: That painting is kept in the national museum.
This book was added to the university library's collection.
The works in the collection number over three thousand.
I heard that an old map is held in the collection.
Experts examine works first before they enter the collection.

examples.ko: 이 유물은 내년부터 새 건물에 소장될 거예요.
examples.en: This relic will be housed in the new building from next year.

explain: '소장'은 박물관·도서관·개인이 귀한 것을 보관하는 것이에요. '보관되다'보다 귀한 작품이나 책에 어울려요. 물건을 모아 두는 쪽은 '소장하다'예요.

phrases.en: I went to see the works kept in the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 박물관 등에서 귀하게 보관하는 작품을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers to valued works held in a museum or similar place.

phrases.example: 그 책은 우리 학교 도서관에 소장되어 있지 않아요.
phrases.en: That book is not in our school library's collection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도서관에 그 자료가 없다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to say a library does not have that item.
phrases.en_equiv: is not held in the collection

phrases.en: This painting is part of the museum's collection.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보관하고 있는 귀한 물건을 부르는 명사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This noun names a valued item that is kept in a collection.

explain_en: '소장' means a museum, library, or individual keeping something valuable. It fits precious works and books more than '보관되다' does. The side that keeps the collection uses '소장하다'.

dis.h: be kept in a museum or collection

en: to be submitted (to an exhibition or contest)

examples.en: That film was entered in a film festival.
My photo will be entered in the contest.

examples.ko: 올해 박람회에는 새 제품이 많이 출품돼요.
examples.en: Many new products are exhibited at this year's expo.
I went and saw all of the submitted works.
That novel could not be entered for the literary prize.
I'm glad my work was entered in the exhibition.

explain: '출품하다'는 내놓는 쪽, '출품되다'는 내놓아지는 쪽 이야기예요. 영화제·공모전·전시회·박람회 앞에 '~에'를 붙여요. 주어는 사진, 영화, 그림 같은 작품이에요. 학교 대회에 낼 때는 보통 '내다', '제출하다'라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 그림은 다음 달 전시회에 출품될 거예요.
phrases.en: That painting will be submitted to the exhibition next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '~에' 앞에 전시회, 영화제 같은 장소나 행사가 와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The event, such as an exhibition or film festival, comes before '에'.
phrases.en_equiv: to be submitted to an exhibition

phrases.en: That work was not submitted to the contest.
phrases.nuance_ko: 작품이 내놓아지지 않았다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says that a work was not entered.

phrases.en: There are a hundred submitted works in total.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대회나 전시에 낸 작품을 가리키는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the works that were entered in a contest or show.

explain_en: '출품하다' is told from the side that puts a work forward, and '출품되다' from the side of the work being put forward. Add '~에' after a film festival, contest, exhibition, or expo. The subject is a work such as a photo, film, or painting. For a school competition people usually say '내다' or '제출하다'.
